summary: Start dates for four Americas residence programmes. Costa Rica: investors became permanent residents under Ley 7033, in force 13 August 1986 (earliest text read). Barbados: the special entry permit dates from 2012 per the US State Department (year only); an industry article gives 1 September 2013 for the US$2m route; no Barbadian legal text found. Quebec and Colombia: no launch date fixed. Quebec's founding regulation could not be read (blocked); Colombia's investor visa traces back at least to Decreto 1000 of 1986 (resident visa from Decreto 666 of 1992), but the 1980 decree it replaced was not read.

events.title: Barbados introduces the special entry permit for high net-worth individuals (US State Department account)
events.description: The US State Department's 2023 Investment Climate Statement says the special entry permit for high net-worth individuals was introduced in 2012. Year only; no legal instrument or in-force date named. A foreign government's account, not a Barbadian text. Other accounts: the 2012 budget announcement (26 June 2012, reported by KPMG) and an effective date of 1 September 2013 for the US$2 million route (reported by IFC Review).
events.location: Section 1 'Openness To, and Restrictions Upon, Foreign Investment', subsection 'Limits on Foreign Control and Right to Private Ownership and Establishment'
events.quote: In 2012, the government introduced a special entry permit for high net-worth individuals who wish to reside in Barbados while working remotely.

events.title: 2012 budget announces special entry permits for high net worth individuals (reported)
events.description: KPMG's summary of the budget delivered on 26 June 2012 lists special entry permits for high net worth individuals (net assets over $10m, currency not stated) and other property owners as a budget measure. An announcement, not an in-force date; the official budget speech was not found. An unofficial summary of a June 2012 Cabinet decision (brb-cabinet-hnwi-sep-2012) says the fees would be cited in that budget speech to give the Immigration Department the legal grounds to implement.
events.quote: Special entry permits (SEPs) to assist HNWI and other property owners who wish to invest in Barbados.

events.title: Five-year special entry permit for owners of US$2 million of property and investments takes effect (reported)
events.description: A Barbadian lawyer's article in IFC Review (February 2015) says that from 1 September 2013 high net worth individuals owning more than US$2 million of Barbados property and investments bought with foreign funds were eligible for a five-year special entry permit. Industry source; no legal instrument named. Recorded as a separate account of the start because it is the only in-force date found for an investment route; the State Department gives 2012.
events.location: Section on the Special Entry Permit programme
events.quote: Effective September 1, 2013, high net worth individuals who own more than US$2 million

events.title: 2015 budget reports the introduction of a Special Entry Permit
events.description: The Minister of Finance's 2015 budget speech lists, among achievements of the Growth and Development Strategy as at 31 March 2015 under 'International Business & Financial Services Sector', the introduction of a Special Entry Permit. Gives no date of introduction.
events.quote: The Government has implemented a multi-year license with IBC’s in addition to the introduction of a Special Entry Permit.

events.title: Quebec introduces its investor programme (reported)
events.description: An investor-program broker's explainer says Quebec introduced its immigrant investor programme in 1986, at the same time as the federal investor class. Industry source, no official text cited; recorded only as a reported account. The Quebec regulation that first created the investor category was not read (see gaps). Not used to fill 'launched'.
events.quote: having introduced the QIIP in 1986 at the same time the Federal Government created the Investor Class

events.title: Decreto 1000 de 1986 provides an ordinary visa for investors (earliest text read; may not be the first)
events.description: Decreto 1000 de 1986, dated 26 March 1986 and applying from its publication (publication date not shown in the text read), provides an 'ordinary visa for investors' valid up to two years for foreigners making a foreign direct investment certified by the Banco de la República; holders of ordinary visas could later get a resident visa after four years. It repealed Decretos 2955 de 1980, 667 de 1981 and 3032 de 1984; Decreto 2955 de 1980 was not read, so investment may have been a route before 1986. Recorded as rule_change, not launch, for that reason. Text read on a private legal database, not an official site.
events.location: Sección Séptima 'Visa ordinaria para inversionistas', arts. 42-43; art. 141
events.quote: podrá expedir visa como inversionista válida hasta por dos (2) años a los extranjeros que vengan al país en tal calidad

events.title: Decreto 666 de 1992 creates a resident visa for investors
events.description: Decreto 666 de 1992 (published in the Diario Oficial 22 April 1992; in force two months after publication under art. 71) lets the resident visa be granted to an 'Inversionista' who contributes capital in amounts set by the Foreign Ministry. Earliest text read giving investors a resident (indefinite) visa directly; it repealed Decreto 1000 de 1986. Date is the publication date.
events.quote: a). Inversionista, para quien aporte capital en los montos que establezca el Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores.

events.title: Ley General de Migración y Extranjería 7033 makes investors a category of permanent resident
events.description: Ley 7033 (sanctioned 4 August 1986, published and in force 13 August 1986: art. 157 'Rige a partir de su publicación' and the Assembly's note 'Rige: 13 8-86') lists 'Inversionistas' among the ways a foreigner may be admitted as a permanent resident. Earliest text read that makes investing a route to Costa Rican residence; Costa Rica's earlier migration rules (before 1986) were not read, so an earlier investor category cannot be ruled out. Later laws (Ley 8487, Ley 8764 of 2009 and its 2012 regulation) moved investors to temporary residence; treated as rule changes to the same programme.
events.location: art. 35 c) (p. 9); art. 157 and closing note (p. 27)
events.quote: Los residentes permanentes podrán ingresar como: a) Inmigrantes, que podrán ser espontáneos, llamados o asistidos. b) Rentistas o pensionados. c) Inversionistas.

gaps: brb-serp: no Barbadian legal text or official notice giving the start date of the special entry permit was found. The official 2012 budget speech (26 June 2012) was not found online (barbadosparliament.com lists load by script); the 2013 budget speech and any Immigration (Amendment) Regulations setting SEP fees were not found. 'launched' = 2012 rests on the US State Department's year-only statement; the 1 September 2013 effective date comes only from an industry article.

brb-serp: legal_basis not filled. The SERP is granted under s.13(3) of the Immigration Act, Cap. 190 (per the Immigration Department form), but no copy of the Act with its commencement date could be read: Refworld returned 403, the SELA copy 404, tradeteam.bb 406. A secondary page dates Cap. 190 to 2 February 1976 (not verified).

can-qc-investor: no official text giving the start of Quebec's investor category was read, so 'launched' is left empty. The 1981 Règlement sur la sélection des ressortissants étrangers (R.R.Q., 1981, c. M-23.1, r. 2) was amended by décrets 2057-84 (19 Sept 1984) and 1080-86 (16 July 1986) among others (listed in décret 590-96, Gazette officielle 29 May 1996); one of these, or the original 1981 text, probably created the investor category, but none was read. BAnQ's digitised Gazette officielle served the 30 July 1986 issue (which does not contain décret 1080-86) and then a CAPTCHA, so no further issues were fetched; LégisQuébec and CanLII returned 403. The 1985 Assemblée nationale committee debates (25 April 1985) already mention 525 'immigrants investisseurs' visas in 1984, but that term then may have meant business immigrants generally.

col-investor-visa: 'launched' left empty. The chain was traced back through Resolución 6045/2017, Decretos 2371/1996, 2268/1995, 2241/1993, 666/1992 (resident visa for investors) and 1000/1986 (two-year ordinary visa for investors). Decreto 1000/1986 repealed Decretos 2955 de 1980, 667 de 1981 and 3032 de 1984; 3032/1984 (read) has no investor rule, but 2955/1980 and 667/1981 were not found online, so investment may have been a route before 1986. Decretos 2107/2001, 4000/2004 and 834/2013 (the links between 1996 and 2017) were not re-read for this pass.

cri-inversionista: Ley 7033 (1986) is the earliest text read. Costa Rica's earlier migration and alien laws (e.g. Ley 1155 of 1950, Ley de Extranjería y Naturalización) and the 1971 Ley 4812 de Residentes Pensionados y Rentistas were not read; whether any pre-1986 text had an investor category is open. Ley 7033 was read from the Assembly's consolidated text (updated to 1999) hosted by Georgetown University, not from La Gaceta of 13 August 1986. legal_basis not applicable/filled.
